$comment: The library pack (F-54): drivers the parts need. Each library has builds: on the Pico W and the ESP32 a driver people already use, as its authors wrote it (unchanged: sha256), its licence beside it; on the micro:bit MicroLab's own, with the same calls, its MIT notice in the file (the micro:bit has about 20 KB for files). files: pack file -> where Add library puts it in the project (on the micro:bit, next to main.py).

libraries.title: HC-SR04 distance
libraries.summary: The distance in cm or mm from an HC-SR04: it sends the trigger pulse and times the echo.

use.pico-w:
from hcsr04 import HCSR04
import time

sensor = HCSR04(trigger_pin=14, echo_pin=13)   # echo through a divider: 5 V becomes 3.3 V
while True:
    print(sensor.distance_cm(), 'cm')
    time.sleep(0.5)
use.esp32-devkit-v1:
from hcsr04 import HCSR04
import time

sensor = HCSR04(trigger_pin=5, echo_pin=18)   # echo through a divider: 5 V becomes 3.3 V
while True:
    print(sensor.distance_cm(), 'cm')
    time.sleep(0.5)

use.microbit-v2:
from microbit import *
from hcsr04 import HCSR04

sensor = HCSR04(trigger_pin=pin1, echo_pin=pin2)   # echo through a divider: 5 V becomes 3.3 V
while True:
    print(sensor.distance_cm(), 'cm')
    sleep(500)

libraries.title: BMP280 air pressure
libraries.summary: The temperature (°C) and air pressure (Pa) from a BMP280 on I²C, with the chip's own calibration.

use.pico-w:
from machine import I2C, Pin
from bmp280 import BMP280
import time

bmp = BMP280(I2C(0, sda=Pin(4), scl=Pin(5)))
bmp.normal_measure()
while True:
    print(bmp.temperature, 'C', bmp.pressure / 100, 'hPa')
    time.sleep(1)
use.esp32-devkit-v1:

from bmp280 import BMP280
import time

bmp = BMP280(I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22)))
bmp.normal_measure()
while True:
    print(bmp.temperature, 'C', bmp.pressure / 100, 'hPa')
    time.sleep(1)

use.microbit-v2:

libraries.title: DS1302 clock
libraries.summary: Sets and reads the time and date on a DS1302 clock, and its 31 bytes of RAM.

use.pico-w:
from machine import Pin
from ds1302 import DS1302
import time

rtc = DS1302(Pin(13), Pin(14), Pin(16))   # CLK, DAT, RST
rtc.date_time([2026, 11, 8, 7, 8, 59, 58])   # year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, second
while True:
    print(rtc.date_time())
    time.sleep(1)
use.esp32-devkit-v1:

from ds1302 import DS1302
import time

rtc.date_time([2026, 11, 8, 7, 8, 59, 58])   # year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, second
while True:
    print(rtc.date_time())
    time.sleep(1)

libraries.title: MPU6050 motion (imu)
libraries.summary: Acceleration (g), turning (°/s) and temperature from an MPU6050 on I²C, as vectors: imu.accel.x, imu.gyro.xyz.

use.pico-w:
from machine import I2C, Pin
from imu import MPU6050
import time

imu = MPU6050(I2C(0, sda=Pin(4), scl=Pin(5)))
while True:
    print('x %.2f y %.2f z %.2f g' % imu.accel.xyz, imu.temperature)
    time.sleep(0.5)

libraries.title: Rotary encoder
libraries.summary: Counts a rotary encoder's steps with pin interrupts, so none are missed while the program does something else.

use.pico-w:
from rotary_irq_rp2 import RotaryIRQ
import time

r = RotaryIRQ(pin_num_clk=14, pin_num_dt=13, min_val=0, max_val=20, range_mode=RotaryIRQ.RANGE_BOUNDED)
last = r.value()
while True:
    if r.value() != last:
        last = r.value()
        print('value', last)
    time.sleep_ms(50)
use.esp32-devkit-v1:
from rotary_irq_esp import RotaryIRQ
import time

r = RotaryIRQ(pin_num_clk=4, pin_num_dt=18, min_val=0, max_val=20, range_mode=RotaryIRQ.RANGE_BOUNDED)
last = r.value()
while True:
    if r.value() != last:
        last = r.value()
        print('value', last)
    time.sleep_ms(50)

use.microbit-v2:
from microbit import *
from rotary import Rotary

r = Rotary(pin8, pin12, min_val=0, max_val=20, range_mode=Rotary.RANGE_BOUNDED)
last = r.value()
while True:
    if r.value() != last:   # read it often: the micro:bit has no pin interrupts
        last = r.value()
        print('value', last)
    sleep(1)

libraries.title: MAX30102 pulse oximeter
libraries.summary: Reads the MAX30102's red and infrared light from its FIFO: the readings a heart rate and SpO2 are worked out from.

builds.authors: Nicola Elia (after SparkFun's MAX3010x library, BSD: its notice is kept in the file)

use.pico-w:
from machine import SoftI2C, Pin
from max30102 import MAX30102

sensor = MAX30102(i2c=SoftI2C(sda=Pin(4), scl=Pin(5), freq=400000))
sensor.setup_sensor()
while True:
    sensor.check()
    if sensor.available():
        print(sensor.pop_red_from_storage(), sensor.pop_ir_from_storage())
